slides.title: Introduction Panel Editor
slides.body:
A panel is a user- configurable
graphical interface. Every control that
can be placed ona panel is called an
element. These elements-buttons,
switches, sliders, and so on – can be
placed anywhere on the panel to
create the look and feel of automotive
control panels.
The Panel Editor is the environment
used for creation and arrangement of
elements for displaying and
controlling variables with values to
be changed, and for assigning
variables to all of these control and
display elemnts.
It’s also possible put text and static
bitmaps on the panel.
IntroductionPanel Editor

slides.title: Introduction Panel Editor
slides.body:
It’s possible interact and change the
values of these variables during
measurement by manipulating the
elements on the panels. The network
node models react to changes in the
variable values and then execute the
appropiate actions (i.e. sending out a
message).
Not only the user can change the
values of the variables, but also CAPL
programs can be used to change this
values when certain events occur.
A clear advantage of using panels is
that they increase your ability to
interpret input and output bus data,
such as on a dashboard. When a node
receives a message, the node can
display the data bounded by the
message onto a panel.
IntroductionPanel Editor

slides.title: Requirements Panel Editor
slides.body:
To use the Panel Editor you must have CANoe.
Panel Editor is a separate application, it can be run in stand-alone mode; however it’s much easier to
create panels in a Panel Editor opened trough CANoe because the variables to be associated with the
elements are in the databases associated to CANoe.
The database has all the variables defined for the elements on the panel, so you will save time and effort
when creating a panels because the Panel Editor recalls the variables defined in the database.
RequirementsPanel Editor

slides.title: Types of variables Panel Editor
slides.body:
The variables that CANoe uses to describe external events are called environment variables and these are
the same variables that can be used to associated with panel elements.
Environment variables can be used both as input and output variables of network nodes, such as sensor
signals and actuator signals.
Environment variables can represent switch positions, temperature, or engine speed. Character string
variables can be used to store text.
Types of variablesPanel Editor

slides.title: Types of variables Panel Editor
slides.body:
Environment variables are defined in the database by the following system parameters:
o Symbolic name of the environment variable
o Value type (i.e. Integer, String, Float, Data)
o Access rights that ECUs have when they access environment variables (i.e. Read – the assigned ECU
can read the environment variable; Write – the assigned ECU can write to the environment variable;
Read/Write – the assigned ECU can read from and write to environment variable
o Unit (physical quantity of the environment variable)
o Initial value (at start of the simulation – only available for environment value type Integer and Float)
o Minimum and maximum of a valid physical value (only available for environment value type Integer and
Float)
o Length of data field in bytes (only for environment variables of value type Data)
Types of variablesPanel Editor

slides.title: Types of variables Panel Editor
slides.body:
It is possible during measurement to manipulate the environment variables by manipulating the controls on
the panels.
The network node will react to the changes to the environment variable and then execute the appropriate
actions (i.e. sending out a message on the bus).
The new value is retrieved by the getVlue () in CAPL
CAPL programs can also change the values of associated anvironment variables when certain event occur
using the putValue () function. The chang e eill visually affect the corresponding element in the panel.
Types of variablesPanel Editor

slides.title: Crating a new panel Panel Editor
slides.body:
There are three methods available to start the Panel Editor:
o The shortcut button on the Canoe toolbar
o The menu command Panel 🡪 Configure panels
o Select a panel in the Configured Panels section of the Panel configuration dialog and then click the Edit
button. This will ensure that the database of your CANoe configuration will be automatically associated to
the Panel Editor.
If you try to open an existing panel for modification, right-click on the title bar of the panel and select Edit.
If the database does not contain the environment variable names associated with the panel’s indicator and
control elements or if there is an element not associated to a variable yet, you will receive a warning
message
Crating a new panelPanel Editor

slides.title: Properties of the Panel Panel Editor
slides.body:
To set the properties of your panel in the Panel Editor, click on the Window Setting button on the toolbar or
select Options 🡪 Window setting.
The first thing your panel needs is a title. This is not just to distinguish each panel from another, but helps
the CANoe operator by displaying the name of the panel on the Windows taskbar at the bottom of the
screen.
CAPL functions like putValueToControl () also need a panel title passed as a parameter to process.
This is also the section in which you can specify the size of the panel, the fonts for each elemnts and the
background color.
Properties of the PanelPanel Editor

slides.title: Elements Panel Editor
slides.body:
Elements allow a variety of value formats to be assigned. In addiction to hexadecimal, decimal, stirng and
bitmaps, symbolic values from CAN database (CANdb file) can be selected and/or displayed on the panel.
The Panel Editor already has a set of pre-defined elements that are ready for use. Each element has a
corresponding button on the toolbar that you can click and place on the panel.
o Control Elements: are used to represent value from a sensor. They can let you change the values
assigned to the environment variables (i.e. switch, push button)
o Display Element: are used to represent values from an actuator and allow let you display changes in the
values assigned to environment variables (i.e. meter, multi-control)
o Static Element: are elements to which no environment variables can be assigned (i.e. label, bitmap)
o I/O Controls: they can be used either to regulate input values resulting from your programmed actions or
to display the resulting output values (i.e. bitmap push button, bitmap switch, value table box etc.)
ElementsPanel Editor

slides.title: Elements configuration Panel Editor
slides.body:
To configure a new element after dragging it
onto the panel, right-click on it and select
Configure this element or just double left-click
on it. This action will open a dialog where you
can specify the value type or data type and the
aspect on the element (i.e. font and background
colour if is possible).
Before an element can be used for input/output,
it must be associated with either an environment
variable or a signal defined in the database. To
do this, select either EnvVar (environment
variable) or Signal from the drop-down list. A list
of available environment variables or signals will
immediately appear in a list selection from which
you can select the environment variable/signal
you want. If the variables/signal you are looking
for is not there, click Select button to find it.

slides.title: Elements configuration Panel Editor
slides.body:
An alarm state is a condition reached when a
value of the panel element goes beyond its
pre-defined maximum or minimum range.
Under such conditions, a visual representation of
that panel element is displayed.
Elements configurationPanel Editor

slides.title: Elements configuration Panel Editor
slides.body:
The Alarm State feature makes it possible for
different panel elements to respond to a situation
in which a value is above or below a previously
defined value range.
It is possible to change the visual representation
of the panel element when a specific value limit
is reached. For example it is possible to respond
to a situation in which a meter value is above or
below a limit by changing colour visualization of
the meter.
Elements configurationPanel Editor

slides.title: Using Bitmaps Panel Editor
slides.body:
Only bitmap (*.bmp) images can be used on panels. Bitmaps reached by right-clicking on the new element
and selecting Configure this element.
Static display usually use a bitmap as a background. Most of the time, bitmaps are used to represent the
state or condition of a variable. These bitmaps are normally used for display purposes, but can be used as
inputs by clicking on the bitmap to change its state. Changing the display state, therefore, changes the value
of the associated environment variable.
The elements that support I/O and bitmaps fall into two categories:
o Two-state elements
o Multi-state elements
Using BitmapsPanel Editor

slides.title: Using Bitmaps Panel Editor
slides.body:
A bitmap file for a two-state element always consists of three separate bitmap pictures. Each with the same
height and width. Arranged to be horizontally adjacent to one another.
The first image appears only when no variables has been assigned to the element, the second one was
used for the logical OFF state, the third one is used for logical state ON.
A bitmap file with n-states consists of n+1 rectangular partial bitmaps of the same height and width,
arranged to be horizontal adjacent.
As for the two-state bitmap file, the first image was used when no variables has been assigned to the
element, the following ones represents the n+1 states of the variables.
Using BitmapsPanel Editor

slides.title: How to associate Panel to CANoe Panel Editor
slides.body:
After the elements on your panel have been configured and saved, they must be associated with the desired
CANoe configuration.
To associate the panels follow this steps:
o Select the menu item Panels 🡪 Configure Panels
o Click Add
o Select your panel (*.cnp)
If the panel has already been added and you made some adjustment using Panel Editor, you do not have
to add the updated panel to CANoe again. The associated panel will automatically update once you’ve
saved it in the Panel Editor.
